summary.headline: KNR Q1 FY27 standalone revenue INR436.7 crore at 15% EBITDA margin, but ~INR46 crore one-off flatters it; underlying margin about 5.5%.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue was INR436.7 crore with EBITDA of INR65 crore (15%) and net profit of INR282.3 crore; consolidated revenue was INR587.9 crore, EBITDA INR96.4 crore (16.4%) and net profit INR80.7 crore. Management said the Q1 margin included a one-off of about INR46 crore (INR76 crore revenue less INR30 crore cost) from the KNR Palani cash surplus EPC claim, and that underlying EBITDA was about 5.5%. Working capital days rose to 133 from 78 at March 2026, and consolidated net debt-to-equity rose to 0.9 from 0.49. Management guided FY27 revenue of INR2,200-2,300 crore at 8-9% EBITDA, with a stronger FY28 and new mining and HAM execution from Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Includes one-off from KNR Palani/Ramagiri sale proceeds

financial_highlights.value: INR46 crore net (INR76 crore revenue less INR30 crore expense)

segments.name: HAM (Hybrid Annuity)
segments.commentary: About 70% of Q1 revenue. Ramanattukara-Valanchery and Valanchery-Kappirikkad at 100%; Marripudi-Somavarappadu ~86%; Magadi-Somwarpet ~91%; Mysore-Kushalnagara Packages 4 and 5 at ~20% and ~18%. INR595 crore of INR805 crore revised equity invested.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: About 25% of Q1 revenue. Water pipeline revenue was only INR7 crore in Q1; INR830 crore pipeline order book, guided INR300-400 crore FY27 execution.

segments.name: Irrigation
segments.commentary: About 3% of Q1 revenue. Unexecuted irrigation book ~INR800 crore; INR825 crore of irrigation book already recognised but unbilled; guided ~INR200 crore FY27 execution. Telangana Package 4 receivables ~INR1,300 crore, total irrigation receivables ~INR1,450 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue INR2,200-2,300 crore (10-15% above FY26's ~INR2,000 crore), with EBITDA ~8-9%.
Q3 and Q4 FY27 EBITDA expected at ~11-12%; FY28 revenue above INR3,000 crore at ~11-12% EBITDA (average 12-13% cited in one answer).
FY27 order inflow target INR8,000-10,000 crore (NHAI, irrigation, state government works).
FY27 capex INR350-400 crore including mining; Kusmunda mining capex ~INR400-450 crore in FY27 per one answer, which conflicts with the company-level figure.

Expects irrigation recovery of INR400-500 crore in FY27 from Telangana, with ~INR650 crore outstanding on Package 4 and a revised estimate of over INR700 crore pending government sanction (5-6 months).
Additional HAM equity of INR210 crore (INR125 crore FY27, INR85 crore FY28), plus possibly ~INR510 crore for Chennai ECR and Telangana HAM.
Buyback under consideration; board decision pending, no size disclosed.
capex_capacity: Kusmunda coal mining (Chhattisgarh, SECL LOA, INR3,361 crore excluding GST, 8 years, with JV partner Sushee Infra): appointed date expected early September 2026 after rains; equipment INR500-600 crore; 100-tonne dumpers due by end-November; Q1 capex nil to INR14 crore.
Banhardih mine (Jharkhand, older award, 5-year contract): only one forest stage cleared; land acquisition 5-6 months; start ~8-10 months away, so likely FY28; equipment INR300-400 crore.
Surface miners cost ~INR13 crore each; four needed initially, up to five if delays.
Mining equipment financing via Caterpillar and Komatsu two-year buyback arrangements (~75% residual value cited), reducing depreciation burden.
demand_pricing: Order book INR8,667 crore excluding 2 new HAM projects and the mining project; INR15,234 crore including them. Mix: roads 38%, irrigation 11%, pipeline 6%, mining 45%.
Client mix: 71% third-party (46% central government, 24% state government, 1% private) and 29% captive HAM.
Order book executable over 3-3.5 years excluding mining; mining 5 and 8 years.
Unbilled order book ~INR1,220 crore (irrigation INR825 crore, others ~INR400 crore). Somvarappadu unexecuted ~INR100 crore vs INR153 crore last quarter.
Railways: FY27 central railway capex INR2.93 lakh crore; Andhra Pradesh railway allocation INR10,134 crore. Metro/MRTS and battery energy storage also evaluated.

Current L1 position ~INR1,500 crore, LOA not yet issued (Chennai and Hyderabad). Bidding in Odisha elevated metro lost on unhealthy pricing; UPEIDA excluded due to greenfield expressway experience requirement.
NHAI FY27 plan to award 54 projects (2,444 km, ~INR1.8 lakh crore); Q1 NHAI awards ~107 km vs ~638 km executed.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 and FY28 execution and revenue look, and when do the two new HAM projects reach appointed date?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue guided at INR2,200-2,300 crore (10-15% above ~INR2,000 crore in FY26), with ECR Chennai, Telangana Mahabubnagar and Kusmunda starting; FY28 targeted above INR3,000 crore. The two new HAM projects are expected to reach appointed date in Q3, and the older Banhardih mine is likely FY28 given 8-10 months to start.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margins are targeted for FY27, FY28 and FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 and Q2 margins to be similar to Q1's; Q3 and Q4 expected at about 11-12%. FY28 average cited at 12-13%, and FY29 at about 8-9% (Q3/Q4 about 10-11%).

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 15% EBITDA margin a one-off, and what is the underlying margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Q1 included about INR90 crore cash surplus EPC claim including GST from the investor deal; net one-off of INR46 crore (INR76 crore revenue less INR30 crore expense). Excluding it, EBITDA margin is around 5.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How much irrigation recovery and Telangana Package 4 payment is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management discussed monthly instalments of about INR70-90 crore, with about INR650 crore outstanding on Package 4 and a revised estimate above INR700 crore pending government sanction over 5-6 months. Analyst's INR400-500 crore FY27 recovery estimate was accepted as expected by management.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed for the Kusmunda and Banhardih mines, and how will depreciation look?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 capex was about INR14 crore. Kusmunda equipment INR500-600 crore; FY27 Kusmunda capex about INR400-450 crore, Banhardih about INR200 crore in FY27 per one answer. Company-level FY27 capex INR350-400 crore. Caterpillar and Komatsu dumpers carry two-year buybacks with about 75% residual value; surface miners and coal equipment are held five to eight years. Management did not give a depreciation figure and targets PAT of 6%-plus on mining.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the buyback and dividend?
qa_highlights.answer: Buyback under consideration; a conclusion meeting is pending and the Board will decide. No size, mechanism or percentage disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split and expected mining and irrigation revenue for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 revenue split: HAM 70%, EPC 25%, irrigation 3%. FY27 irrigation about INR200 crore from ~INR800 crore unexecuted book; pipeline INR300-400 crore; mining about INR150 crore in FY27 (INR20-40 crore slippage risk) and about INR400 crore in FY28 from Kusmunda, with Banhardih possibly INR500 crore a year if it starts.

qa_highlights.question: What unbilled order book and Somvarappadu and Mysore-Kushalnagara exposure exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Unbilled order book about INR1,220 crore (irrigation INR825 crore, others about INR400 crore). Somvarappadu unexecuted about INR100 crore versus INR153 crore last quarter. Mysore-Kushalnagara Packages 4 and 5 are expected to be completed by April-May 2027, with partial COD by December on land available.

risks_watch: Q1 margin of 15% is inflated by a one-off of about INR46 crore net; underlying margin about 5.5%, so H2 guidance of 11-12% EBITDA depends on HAM and mining ramp-up.
Telangana Package 4 recovery: about INR650 crore outstanding plus a revised estimate above INR700 crore pending government sanction over 5-6 months; receivables total about INR1,450 crore irrigation.
Working capital days rose to 133 from 78 at March 2026 and consolidated net debt-to-equity rose to 0.9 from 0.49, with consolidated debt at INR1,975 crore.

Kusmunda mining start depends on appointed date (expected early September) amid monsoon haul-road delays; 100-tonne dumpers due by end-November. Banhardih timing uncertain (likely FY28) due to forest and land approvals.

Mining capex inconsistencies on the call: FY27 Kusmunda capex cited as INR400-450 crore in one answer versus company-level INR350-400 crore; mining depreciation and EBITDA not yet quantified by management.

Order inflow target INR8,000-10,000 crore for FY27 against Q1 NHAI awards of about 107 km versus about 638 km executed; L1 of about INR1,500 crore awaiting LOA; UPEIDA excluded for lack of greenfield expressway experience; battery storage bids seen as risky.
Additional HAM equity of INR210 crore plus possibly about INR510 crore for Chennai ECR and Telangana HAM; buyback size and mechanism still undecided.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the long-term order book, FY28 growth and mining economics, but cautious and vague on near-term specifics such as Telangana recovery timing, mining EBITDA and depreciation, buyback size, and battery storage bids, often deferring to future board decisions.
